instruments.evidence: MarkGroupKeyStale at every membership change: AddGroupParticipant, RemoveGroupParticipant and LeaveGroup on the pool; AcceptGroupInvite and BanGroupMember inside their own transactions. The integration test router gained the participant, leave and ban routes, and the integration test drives each path.
800d8e003 (G1b ledger, which added the routes), a848b585c (G1a: the service and MarkGroupKeyStale).
The key state JSON after each membership change: active_version 0 after a join, a removal, a leave and a ban; back to the stored version after each rotation.
Every path driven over HTTP: POST participants 201, DELETE participant 204, POST leave 204, POST ban 200, and the key state read between each.
The rows behind those answers: the active version ends (is_active FALSE) while every stored copy stays, so members keep reading the history they already hold.
MarkGroupKeyStale takes the same handle the surrounding code already uses: the pool where the change is a single statement, the transaction where it is not.
The handlers pass the conversation id they already validated; the service decides everything else.
One function ends a version, called from five places; no handler writes that SQL itself.
The test group and its members are built as CreateGroup builds them, through the real routes for every change.
A join, an invite acceptance, a removal, a leave and a ban each end the version.
A failed membership change writes nothing: the invite and ban paths do both inside one transaction.
A removal that matches no row answers 404 before anything is marked stale.
Sibling paths compared: every place that writes conversation_participants now ends the version; CreateGroup needs none, since a group has no version before its first rotation.

Branch by branch: the join, removal and leave paths were driven by the new test, but the ban hook in group_admin.go was reached by nothing, because the integration router registered no ban route. An untested hook in its own transaction is exactly where a later edit drops the call (g1c-ban-leaves-the-key-version-active).
A failed MarkGroupKeyStale is not swallowed: each call answers 500 (the ban path also logs with its handler prefix) instead of reporting a membership change whose key version still stands.
The rule lives in the service; the handlers only call it.

Shape 'a membership change that forgets the key': grepped every INSERT INTO and DELETE FROM conversation_participants in the handlers; all five now end the version, and CreateGroup is the documented exception.
No shared state; the service serialises rotations.
The invite and ban paths mark the version stale inside the same transaction as the membership row, so a rollback undoes both.
Ending a version keeps every stored copy: a member who leaves keeps what it could already read, and reads nothing new.
Control built after the fix; see pass 2.
gofmt clean, go build ./... ok, go vet ok with and without the integration tag, golangci-lint 0 issues; the membership and routes tests passed, and the handlers package passed (263s).
E2 names it; no new instrument.
Fed the rule the thing it exists to refuse: with the ban hook removed the test fails, so the check is not blind; and a removal that matches no row still answers 404 without ending a version.
Every run reported 0 SKIP.
The approved G plan: a join or a leave ends the version, and the next sender makes the next one for exactly the current members. G1c is that rule, wired to every membership path.
One call per path.
The changed handlers were exercised by the whole handlers package and by the integration tests that drive their routes.
